decisions.reason: As a core airfield-lighting control product in a growing airport-technology market, it fits the firm's established systems business and still offers option value that likely exceeds its carrying cost.

This surveillance display extends the existing airport-operations portfolio, and with no clear evidence of failure the firm would likely preserve the option while adoption uncertainty continues to resolve.
A training program has low carrying cost and supports the installed base, so management is likely to keep it as a cheap complementary option around core systems sales.

Although its weaker website prominence suggests more limited traction, it is a low-cost training offer tied to the firm's lighting business, so keeping it still looks better than dropping it outright.

Collaboration software is closely aligned with the firm's strategic move toward integrated and intelligent airport operations, and software-like offerings are relatively cheap to keep while market potential unfolds.

The multilateration system is a strategic surveillance product with longer airport sales cycles, so despite higher support and engineering costs the firm would likely retain it until demand becomes clearer.
